node.label: Anthony Pagden
node.date_label: The Fall of Natural Man (1982) · European Encounters with the New World (1993) · Lords of All the World (1995)
node.description: An intellectual historian of empire and international political ideas. His interview connects European self-understanding to overseas encounters and distinguishes the modern project of European union from an empire, while stating his own cosmopolitan and progress-oriented commitments.

people_update.label: Anthony Pagden
people_update.identity_note: Anthony Pagden, historian identified by The Fall of Natural Man and European Encounters with the New World. Distinctive work concordance establishes this new identity; no authority QID assigned.

proposed_edges.relationship: Studies European political self-understanding through ideas of empire and relations with peoples outside Europe.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview relates Hispanic/Amerindian encounters to European categories, not simply Spanish national ideas.

proposed_edges.relationship: Connects projects of European unity with imperial experience and changing international arrangements.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview distinguishes Europe’s aggregate of states from empire, while acknowledging imperial preservation as part of the history. His cosmopolitan-progressive evaluation remains his position.
